zakatClaimEvidence: Muslim Aid USA's website explicitly states: "An annual obligation, Zakat is given by eligible adult Muslims whose wealth exceeds the Nisab threshold for a full lunar year. It directs essential support to those in need, both locally and across the globe." Additionally, their website features a dedicated 'Zakat' section with a 'Zakat Guide,' 'Zakat Calculator,' and 'Zakat Appeal,' stating, 'Support verified recipients in need through our Zakat distribution program. Verified Recipients. 8 Eligible Categories. Transparent Process. Regular Updates. Donate Zakat.' Their 'Donation Policy' also includes an 'IMPORTANT NOTE REGARDING CREDIT CARD DONATIONS FOR ZAKAT.' (Source: https://www.mausa.org/religious-dues/zakat/)

In FY2024, the organization managed <cite id="3">Total Revenue of $26,971,910</cite> to support victims of conflict and natural disasters globally. The charity operates with <cite id="1">high fundraising efficiency, spending only $0.04 per $1 raised</cite> to secure operational funding. They maintain an overall <cite id="3">Program expense ratio of 84.2%</cite>. When excluding noncash gifts-in-kind, the organization maintains a <cite id="3">Cash-Adjusted Program expense ratio of 84.2%</cite>, which exceeds the 75% industry benchmark and demonstrates efficient deployment of financial gifts. Muslim Aid America is <cite id="2">ZAKAT-ELIGIBLE</cite> and distributes funds according to traditional Islamic criteria across multiple <cite id="2">asnaf categories including fuqara and masakin</cite>. Their work heavily focuses on emergency capacity building and relief efforts across Asia, Africa, and the Middle East.
